replication.target_description: Study 1, non-direct replication in French-speaking computer users: confirmatory omnibus three-condition ANOVA of absolute moral-judgment deviation from midpoint 4; no age/gender covariates.

n.sample_role: participants using computers in the confirmatory Study 1 ANOVA
n.exclusions: From 12,335 collected participants, excluded 13 who answered no questions and restricted primary analysis to computer users; touchpad and smartphone users excluded from the primary sample. Additional age exclusions apply only to exploratory covariate analyses, not this target test.

reported_success.location: article p. 5 (HAL PDF p. 6), section 2.2.4 Discussion
reported_success.quote: Unfortunately, we were unable to observe that priming a black-and-white (as opposed to blue-and-yellow or gray) background could significantly influence the perception of a moral judgment, and lead to polarization.

notes: Both primary full papers were retrieved and their titles/DOIs verified. Original target is the omnibus effect on judgment polarization (partial eta-squared .07), rather than its separate pairwise contrasts. Replication uses the matching Study 1 confirmatory omnibus analysis; it is explicitly described by its authors as a non-direct replication owing to French-language materials and preceding questionnaire battery. Printed replication partial eta-squared is an upper bound, retained verbatim. Original n is reported in Method and supported by the ANOVA degrees of freedom; no exclusions are documented. HAL adds a cover page, so article page numbers differ from PDF positions by one for the replication.
